title: Shallow vs deep foundations
examples: What is the difference between shallow and deep foundations?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: The soil and the load decide which is needed

explain.say: All foundations do the same job: pass a building's weight into the ground without it sinking. Engineers choose between shallow and deep foundations depending on the soil and the load.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: The soil and the load decide which is needed

explain.say: Shallow foundations sit just below the surface. Pads under columns, strips under walls, or a raft under the whole building spread the load over firm soil, like snowshoes on snow.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: The soil and the load decide which is needed

explain.say: Deep foundations are needed when the top soil is soft or the building is very heavy. Piles or caissons carry the load down, sometimes tens of metres, to firmer soil or rock.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: The soil and the load decide which is needed

explain.say: Before choosing, engineers drill boreholes to test the ground. A house on firm clay may need only strip footings, while a skyscraper on soft ground needs hundreds of piles.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: The soil and the load decide which is needed

faq.a: The ground under a building can only take so much pressure before it sinks. Foundations spread the load or carry it down to stronger ground, so the building does not settle or tilt.
Shallow foundations are pads, strips or rafts just below ground level. They spread the load over a wide area of firm soil and suit houses and light buildings.
Deep foundations are piles or caissons that reach down through weak soil to firmer layers. They carry load by resting on the hard layer at their tip and by friction along their sides.
asks: When do you need deep foundations?

faq.q: How do engineers know what the ground is like?
faq.a: They drill boreholes, take soil samples and test how strong and how squashy each layer is. This site investigation decides the foundation design.

faq.q: What happens if foundations are wrong?
faq.a: The building can settle unevenly, crack or tilt. The Leaning Tower of Pisa leans because its shallow foundation sits on soft ground that squashed more on one side.
asks: Why does the Leaning Tower of Pisa lean?

facts: The Leaning Tower of Pisa began to tilt during construction in the late 1100s because its shallow foundation rests on soft soil.
A raft foundation spreads a building's load over its whole footprint, which lowers the pressure on the soil.

quiz.say: A tall office block is planned on 20 metres of soft clay above solid rock. What foundation does it most likely need?
quiz.show: Tall block on soft clay over rock needs…
quiz.why: Piles carry the heavy load through the soft clay to the strong rock beneath.

wrong.1: Shallow pads would press on soft clay, which would squash and let the building sink.
wrong.2: Every building needs a foundation to pass its load into the ground.
